targetTexts.1: On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.
targetTexts.2: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
targetTexts.3: but when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
targetTexts.4: While they were puzzling over this, suddenly two men in radiant apparel stood beside them.
targetTexts.5: As the women bowed their faces to the ground in terror, the two men asked them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?
targetTexts.6: He is not here; He has risen! Remember how He told you while He was still in Galilee:
targetTexts.7: ‘The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.’”
targetTexts.9: And when they returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the Eleven and to all the others.
targetTexts.10: It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told this to the apostles.
targetTexts.11: But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.
targetTexts.12: Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb. And after bending down and seeing only the linen cloths, he went away, wondering to himself what had happened.
targetTexts.13: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.
targetTexts.14: They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.
targetTexts.15: And as they talked and deliberated, Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.
targetTexts.16: But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.
targetTexts.17: He asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?” They stood still, with sadness on their faces.
targetTexts.18: One of them, named Cleopas, asked Him, “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?”
targetTexts.19: “What things?” He asked. “The events involving Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered. “This man was a prophet, powerful in speech and action before God and all the people.
targetTexts.20: Our chief priests and rulers delivered Him up to the sentence of death, and they crucified Him.
targetTexts.21: But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is the third day since these things took place.
targetTexts.22: Furthermore, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning,
targetTexts.23: but they did not find His body. They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.
targetTexts.24: Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had described. But Him they did not see.”
targetTexts.25: Then Jesus said to them, “O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
targetTexts.26: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?”
targetTexts.27: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.
targetTexts.28: As they approached the village where they were headed, He seemed to be going farther.
targetTexts.29: But they pleaded with Him, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.” So He went in to stay with them.
targetTexts.30: While He was reclining at the table with them, He took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to them.
targetTexts.31: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus—and He disappeared from their sight.
targetTexts.32: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
targetTexts.33: And they got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem. There they found the Eleven and those with them, gathered together
targetTexts.34: and saying, “The Lord has indeed risen and has appeared to Simon!”
targetTexts.35: Then the two told what had happened on the road, and how they had recognized Jesus in the breaking of the bread.
targetTexts.36: While they were describing these events, Jesus Himself stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
targetTexts.37: But they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit.
targetTexts.38: “Why are you troubled,” Jesus asked, “and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
targetTexts.39: Look at My hands and My feet. It is I Myself. Touch Me and see—for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.”
targetTexts.40: And when He had said this, He showed them His hands and feet.
targetTexts.41: While they were still in disbelief because of their joy and amazement, He asked them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
targetTexts.42: So they gave Him a piece of broiled fish,
targetTexts.43: and He took it and ate it in front of them.
targetTexts.44: Jesus said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”
targetTexts.45: Then He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
targetTexts.46: And He told them, “This is what is written: The Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
targetTexts.47: and in His name repentance and forgiveness of sins will be proclaimed to all nations, beginning in Jerusalem.
targetTexts.48: You are witnesses of these things.
targetTexts.49: And behold, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you. But remain in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high.”
targetTexts.50: When Jesus had led them out as far as Bethany, He lifted up His hands and blessed them.
targetTexts.51: While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven.
targetTexts.52: And they worshiped Him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
targetTexts.53: praising God continually in the temple.
